abstract: Transcription factors (TFs) recognize DNA through well-defined DNA-binding domains, but their regulatory output depends on effector domains that activate or repress transcription. Most effector domains have been mapped one protein at a time in low-throughput reporter assays, and the resulting annotations remain scattered across decades of literature. We present TFRegDB v2.0, a curated database of experimentally supported transcriptional effector domains resolved at the level of individual protein isoforms. By combining language-model-assisted screening of the published literature with manual verification of every record, and merging these annotations with high-throughput domain-mapping screens, we consolidated 5277 experimentally supported domain reports across 1268 human TFs from 64 families, curated from 1072 publications and representing an 8.7-fold expansion over our previous compendium. Every activation and repression domain annotation is delivered together with precomputed AlphaFold structural models, per-residue conservation at amino acid and nucleotide resolution, computational predictions, short linear motifs, biophysical and disorder profiles, post-translational modifications, germline variants, and the exon-intron structure encoding the domain, allowing users to evaluate how alternative isoforms and genetic variation compromise effector-domain integrity. TFRegDB v2.0 is freely accessible through an interactive portal, a public REST API and bulk downloads at https://tfregdb.com, and accepts community-submitted annotations for future releases.
